tier_reason: Two independent WebSearch summaries of the abstract (Edamatsu and Takahashi, ICA3PP 2019, Springer LNCS chapter 10.1007/978-3-030-38991-8_5) give 'up to approximately 3.07 times faster than AVX-512F and approximately 2.97 times faster than GMP' on Cannon Lake. The paper is peer-reviewed, which would justify B, but semanticscholar, Springer and ACM are egress-blocked, so it was never opened and the numbers are snippet only; the harness caps snippet-only evidence at C, and no code was found.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Up to about 3.07x faster than the authors' own AVX-512F implementation and about 2.97x faster than GMP for large-integer multiplication on a Cannon Lake CPU (abstract as quoted in WebSearch summaries; paper not opened).
corrections.workload: Large-integer multiplication using Intel AVX-512IFMA (52-bit multiply-add, reduced-radix representation with the spare 12 bits used to accumulate carries) on a Cannon Lake processor, compared with the authors' AVX-512F implementation and with GMP.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the paper (ICA3PP 2019, Springer LNCS, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-38991-8_5; also indexed on semanticscholar and ResearchGate) could not be opened because semanticscholar, link.springer.com, dl.acm.org and researchgate are egress-blocked. The 3.07x/2.97x figures and the attribution to this paper are now confirmed by two separate search summaries of its abstract, and both are 'up to' (best-case) ratios. Peer-reviewed venue, so a verifier who can open the paper may re-tier to B. GMP version, operand sizes, compiler, flags and exact CPU model are unknown; GMP has no AVX-512 kernels, so the baseline is presumably its scalar x86-64 mpn code. Cannon Lake was a short-lived, discontinued microarchitecture (IFMA now ships on Ice Lake and later Intel cores and on AMD Zen 4/5). No public code found (WebSearch for code and PDF copies on GitHub turned up nothing attributable), so has_code=false.

notes: Real peer-reviewed result; numbers and attribution confirmed via search summaries only, so it stays C; candidate for a B retier once springer/semanticscholar is reachable. A search summary also mentioned an Intel Core i3-8121U, but my query contained that model name, so hardware was left uncorrected. Shortcomings to record: no public code, snippet-only evidence, best-case 'up to' ratios, discontinued test CPU.

tier_reason: Same arXiv 2604.21566 preprint ('Leveraging SIMD for Accelerating Large-number Arithmetic') as the already-verified entry paper:digitsonturbo-dot, which a previous verifier opened and held at C (no public code, only an anonymous.4open.science review link; preprint without a stated venue). arXiv is egress-blocked here; the snippet figures match that entry.
notes: Same work as paper:digitsonturbo-dot: DoTMP is the paper's name for DoT patched into GMP 6.3.0 (DoTSSL is the OpenSSL 3.5.2 variant), so file this as decision duplicate of that entry. A WebSearch summary confirms the GMPbench +7.8% overall, pi +19.3% and multiplication +48.7% figures (the division +8.4% figure is already in the known entry's enrichment); the known entry's claimed_speedup could add the GMPbench +7.8% figure. Code is still only at anonymous.4open.science/r/DigitsOnTurbo, with no GitHub repo found.

tier_reason: WebSearch summaries of the abstract of 'Acceleration of Large Integer Multiplication with Intel AVX-512 Instructions' (Edamatsu and Takahashi, IEEE HPCC 2018, ieeexplore document 8622797) say it compares execution time and instruction counts with GMP and is 'approximately 2.5x faster than GMP' on Knights Landing. Peer-reviewed, but ieeexplore and semanticscholar are egress-blocked, so the evidence is snippet only and capped at C; no code is attributable to the paper.

corrections.claimed_speedup: About 2.5x faster execution time than GMP for large-integer multiplication on Knights Landing using AVX-512F (abstract as quoted in WebSearch summaries; paper not opened).
corrections.workload: Large-integer multiplication with AVX-512F instructions in a reduced-radix representation on the Knights Landing Xeon Phi, comparing execution time and instruction counts with GMP.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the paper (2018 IEEE 20th International Conference on High Performance Computing and Communications, HPCC; ieeexplore document 8622797) could not be opened because ieeexplore and semanticscholar are egress-blocked. The 2.5x figure and its attribution to this paper are now confirmed by two separate search summaries of the abstract. Operand sizes, GMP version, compiler, flags and exact Xeon Phi model are unknown; GMP has no AVX-512 kernels, and Knights Landing's scalar cores are weak, so the win over GMP is specific to that platform. Knights Landing (Xeon Phi) is discontinued. Peer-reviewed venue, so a verifier with paper access may re-tier to B. The GitHub repo Hibari-K/bigint_mul_avx512f (C intrinsics, Makefile targets Knights Landing with -xMIC-AVX512, 28-bit limb splitting, commits 2017-2019, no license, 1 star) matches the topic and period, but nothing in it names the authors or the paper and it has no GMP comparison, so it is not attributed and has_code stays false.

notes: Real peer-reviewed result; stays C because the paper could not be opened.
